title: The Lantean protocol, revision 1
description: JSON Schema for every CORE-OWNED control frame and the data-event envelope of the Lantean protocol (PROTOCOL.md). Additional properties are permitted everywhere: the protocol is forward-compatible and a peer ignores fields it does not recognize (PROTOCOL.md section 10). The same rule holds at the frame level: an unrecognized application control frame passes through to the application handler, and higher layers define their own frames that way (svelte-realtime ships its companion schema as svelte-realtime/protocol.schema.json). A validator for mixed ecosystem traffic accepts a frame when it matches the core schema OR a composed layer schema. A core frame is one of the definitions in $defs; correlate control frames by their `type` const. The x-webtransport annotation carries the non-JSON carriage constants from PROTOCOL.md sections 14.7 and 15; that binding is a freeze candidate (see the Meta section's Additive additions), so these constants are provisional until its wire-status line reads frozen. Record size splits into two obligations because nothing on that carriage negotiates a size: maximumSenderMessageBytes is what a sender may emit unnegotiated, and defaultReceiverMessageBytes is what a receiver accepts absent configuration, which a deployment SHOULD move in step with its WebSocket limit in either direction (receiverMessageBytesConfigurable), so one deployment does not accept a message on one carriage and refuse it on the other. innerControlFrameCeilingBytes restates the core section 1.2 constant, which is not stream-specific but does keep applying after deframing, and only client-to-server as in that section. minimumPendingBytes is a floor on the send-queue bound, which must also cover the largest record this endpoint may itself emit. maximumLengthPrefixBytes caps the prefix parse at 5 groups, so no length above 34359738367 is expressible and a receiver decides on the complete prefix rather than a partial value. Each record carries one kind byte between the length prefix and the message bytes (recordKindBytes), restating the WebSocket text/binary opcode the byte stream itself discards; recordKinds registers the values, and both an unregistered kind and an invalid-UTF-8 text record are structural rejections with the named stream errors rather than pass-through, because a record whose type is unknown cannot be delivered anywhere safely. Neither the prefix nor the kind byte counts toward pending-byte accounting.

ref.description: Client-allocated correlation id: a number or a string.

reconnect.description: Server -> client drain advisory: the node is draining/restarting and asks the client to reconnect on a jittered schedule in [afterMs, afterMs+windowMs), so a fleet does not stampede the replacement. Additive and unknown-type-safe (an old client ignores it).

game.description: Client -> server client-driven relay publish (the `game` lane, PROTOCOL.md section 3.10). Carries NO topic: the server derives it from the connection's publish grant. `event` is a string; `data` is any JSON value; `id` is an optional client-chosen input id echoed on the fan-out.

game-denied.description: Server -> the sender of a rejected `game` frame (PROTOCOL.md section 3.10). `FORBIDDEN`: no publish grant. `INVALID`: granted but a malformed frame (non-string event). `id` is echoed when the rejected frame carried one.

message-overloaded.description: Server -> client response for an application message shed by established-message admission (PROTOCOL.md section 3.11). Rate overflow includes retryAfterMs; concurrency/queue overflow does not imply the message was retained.

data-event.description: The published-event carrier. No `type` field: identified by `topic` + `event`. `id` appears only on the fan-out of a `game`-lane frame (section 3.10), echoing the sender's input id.
